newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Iraq links oil price formula to oil-for-food deal.
newsitem.headline: Iraq links oil price formula to oil-for-food deal.

text.p: Iraq has said it would not go ahead with the oil-for-food plan until the U.N. Security Council's sanction committee agreed on an oil-pricing formula, a senior U.N. official said on Wednesday.

"Iraq has conveyed to us very recently that the question of a pricing mechanism or pricing formula is of primary importance for Iraq. Unless the pricing formula is settled, Iraq cannot move ahead with the implementation of 986," said Under-Secretary-General Chinmaya Gharekhan.
The pricing formula by which Iraq will be allowed to sell oil in exchange for humanitarian goods is determined by the sanctions committee and changes each month.

Gharekhan said that Iraq would shortly present another pricing formula proposal as it had not submitted one to the committee since August. The United States earlier had objected to some aspects of the pricing formula but diplomats had said the question was moot since the entire deal was on hold for other reasons.

The oil-for-food deal allows Iraq to sell $2 billion of oil over six months, on a renewable basis, to buy food, medicine and other necessities to help offset the effect on ordinary Iraqis of sanctions imposed after Iraq's August 1990 invasion of Kuwait.

Gharekhan indicated there was no progress on earlier Iraqi demands that were unacceptable to the United Nations. These included curtailing the freedom of movement of U.N. personnel and for new local U.N. staff to be hired to replace those already working for the United Nations.

Arrangements to launch the plan were close to completion when Iraqi President Saddam Hussein sent troops into the largely Kurdish-inhabited north of the country at the end of August to back one side in an inter-Kurdish conflict.
Asked how he assessed the Security situation in Iraq, Gharekhan said: "We have so many other issues to settle now. So we will see about that one later."
